description: Analyze a TypeScript/JavaScript project for unused code and dependency cycles. On a Rust root, it runs `cargo fallow check` (deps, visibility; no score) and takes only root. Detects unused files, exports, types, dependencies, enum/class members, unresolved imports, unlisted dependencies, duplicate exports, circular dependencies, re-export cycles (barrel files that form a structural loop, silently breaking re-exports), package cycles (workspace packages that import each other in a loop), boundary violations, rule-pack policy violations (banned calls, imports, and catalogue-derived effects declared via the rulePacks config key), stale suppression comments, missing suppression reasons when rules.require-suppression-reason is enabled, unused pnpm catalog entries (entries in pnpm-workspace.yaml `catalog:` / `catalogs:` not referenced by any workspace package), empty pnpm catalog groups, unresolved catalog references (workspace package.json declares `catalog:` but the catalog has no entry), unused dependency overrides (entries in `pnpm-workspace.yaml#overrides`, `package.json#pnpm.overrides`, top-level `package.json#overrides`, or Bun `package.json#resolutions` whose target package no workspace package declares and the active readable lockfile does not resolve), and misconfigured dependency overrides (unparsable key or empty value; the active package manager may reject or ignore the entry). Opt-in issue_types: "private-type-leaks", "deprecated-exports-in-use", "absent-component-props", "constant-parameters", "namespace-escapes", "test-only-exports". Returns structured JSON with all issues found, grouped by issue type. Each finding has a stable `finding_id`; an id absent from a scoped or differently configured run means unknown, not resolved. For code duplication use find_dupes, for complexity hotspots use check_health. Supports baselines, regression detection, performance tuning, boundary_violations, and group_by. Read the `fallow://tools/analyze` resource for the boundary_violations alias, the group_by modes, and how to dispatch the `next_steps[]` follow-up commands.

allow_remote_extends.description:
Allow trusted HTTPS config `extends` for this request. Defaults to false
and never grants process-global trust.

baseline.description:
Compare results against a saved baseline file. Only new issues (not in
the baseline) are reported. The response carries `baseline_staleness`:
read `gate_trips` to see whether the baseline has entries that match
nothing any more (re-save it with `save_baseline`), and read
`change_scoped` first, because a run narrowed to part of the project can
report `matched_entries: 0` on a perfectly healthy baseline.
`scope_reasons` names the channels that narrowed it.
`unrecognised_format: true` means the file is not this command's baseline.
It suppressed nothing, so use another path and do not re-save.
`saved_by` then names the command that wrote it, when fallow knows it.

config.description: Path to a fallow config file.

fail_on_regression.description:
Fail if the issue count increased beyond `tolerance` compared to a
regression baseline.

file.description: Scope analysis to these project-relative files instead of the whole project.

finding_ids.description:
Report only these `finding_id` values. The response adds
`finding_id_query`; a missing id is resolved only when `conclusive` is true.

group_by.description:
Group findings by CODEOWNERS ownership, directory, workspace package, or
GitLab CODEOWNERS section. Values: "owner", "directory", "package", "section".

include_entry_exports.description: Report unused exports in entry files instead of auto-marking them as used.

issue_types.description:
Issue types to include, for example `["unused-exports", "unused-files"]`;
empty or omitted means all registered issue types.

no_package_baselines.description:
Ignore the per-package refs of `workspaces.changedSince` for this call,
so every workspace package is analyzed in full scope. Use it to judge
or save a whole-project baseline.

production.description:
Production mode: exclude test, story, and dev files, only start/build
scripts, and report type-only dependencies.

regression_baseline.description: Path to the regression baseline file.

root.description: Project root; defaults to the working directory.

save_baseline.description:
Save current results as a baseline file for future comparisons. The path
must resolve inside the project root, its Git work tree, the CI workspace or a temp directory.
A relative path resolves against the working directory of the MCP
server, not against `root`, so pass an absolute path.

save_regression_baseline.description:
Save the current issue counts as a regression baseline file at this
path. An empty or absent value writes nothing: this tool cannot write the
counts into the fallow config. The path must resolve inside the project
root, its Git work tree, the CI workspace or a temp directory.
A relative path resolves against the working directory of the MCP
server, not against `root`, so pass an absolute path.

show_cascade.description:
Keep the unused exports, types, class members and enum members of
unused files. By default the report hides them and counts them in
`cascade_hidden`. Passed through to the CLI's `--show-cascade` flag.

threads.description: Parser thread count; defaults to CPU cores.

tolerance.description: Allowed issue count increase before a regression is flagged. Defaults to "0".

type_aware.description:
Refine project-wide public API findings with TypeScript symbol identity.
`false` keeps the run syntactic, also when the config turns type-aware analysis on. `type_aware_projects` or `type_aware_require` turns it on and wins over `false`.

type_aware_projects.description: Explicit tsconfig paths for type-aware analysis.

type_aware_require.description: Whether incomplete semantic evidence is advisory or gating.

workspace.description: Workspace packages to analyze: name or repo-relative path, comma-separated list, globs, `!` negation.

name: analyze
